questions.questionText: Extract C (lines 6–7) states: ‘An alternative would be to impose a maximum price for consumers, as both Sri Lanka and the Philippines have done’. Using the data and your knowledge of economics, evaluate the view that imposing a maximum price for rice is the best way for a rice-importing nation, such as Nigeria, to ensure the affordability of a basic food for its citizens.
Which one of the following is most likely to indicate that a government is trying to cause a significant change in the pattern of economic activity?
options: A reduction in the rate of tax on income from retirement pensions
A reduction in the tax on a good with positive consumption externalities
An increase in the rate of an inheritance tax
An increase in the tax on a good with very inelastic demand

questions.questionText: A government announces that, over a 10 year period, it plans to reduce the number of tradable pollution permits it issues each year. Which one of the following is the most likely response from firms in industries affected by the announcement?
options: Firms are likely to delay investment into more environmentally friendly production methods
Only the firms that generate the most pollution are likely to react at all
Over time, more firms will have an incentive to reduce their pollution
The firms with the lowest costs of reducing pollution will buy the most permits

questions.questionText: After considering Extract D, and the original evidence in Extracts A, B and C, would you recommend that the Government continue to subsidise firms to encourage them to set up gigafactories to produce batteries in the UK? Justify your recommendation.

Extract C (lines 14–16) states that ‘A maximum rent can help keep the cost of student accommodation lower than it would otherwise be, but risks some landlords withdrawing from the market’. Using the data in the extracts and your knowledge of economics, discuss the advantages and disadvantages of policies the government might introduce to improve the market for student accommodation.

Figure 2 shows the original demand (D) and supply (S) curves for pints of milk. To help farmers, the government introduces a minimum price of 80p for a pint of milk. Which one of the following is most likely to result from the imposition of this minimum price?
options: Profits of farmers from selling milk will increase by £1 million
The revenue received by farmers will increase by 30p per pint
There will be excess demand of 40 million pints
Total revenue from the sales of milk will increase by £100 million

questions.questionText: Technological change has made it easier to charge for road use, including charging road users different prices according to demand at different times of the day. Which one of the following would be the most likely outcome if the government introduced variable charges, according to the time of day, for using motorways in the UK?
options: Fewer people will use trains to go to work.
More vehicles will use motorways at busy times.
Motorways would become a public good.
The costs of many businesses will increase.

questions.questionText: Figure 3 shows the demand (D) and supply (S) curves for a good in a market. The diagram shows a shift of the supply curve for the good from S1 to S2 caused by the removal of a subsidy. All other things being equal, which one of the following is the most likely consequence of this action?
options: A change in the pattern of economic activity
A decrease in the budget surplus
A reduction in the balance of payments deficit
An increase in direct tax revenue

questions.questionText: Extract B (lines 20–21) states that ‘all vehicle owners should be forced to pay the full costs of their driving. This would incentivise people to consider using public transport, cycling or walking.’ Evaluate policies that could be used to reduce the environmental impact of all types of car.

A government sets a maximum price for fruit below the market price to try to encourage healthier eating. All other things being equal, which one of the following will result in the lowest amount of excess demand for fruit at the maximum price?
options: Demand is income elastic and supply is price elastic.
Demand is income inelastic and supply is price inelastic.
Demand is price elastic and supply is price elastic.
Demand is price inelastic and supply is price inelastic.

questions.questionText: Figure 4 shows the free market demand (D1) and supply (S) curves for a merit good. D2 is the demand curve if all the benefits from consuming the good are taken into account. Which one of the following government policies would be most likely to achieve the socially optimal level of consumption?
options: A maximum price of P3
A minimum price of P2
A subsidy of P1 minus P3 per unit
A subsidy of P2 minus P3 per unit

questions.questionText: A government decides to increase its subsidy to rail services to encourage more people to travel by rail. The subsidy is most likely to be successful if rail travel has a
options: demand that is elastic with respect to price.
demand that is inelastic with respect to price.
high positive income elasticity of demand.
negative cross elasticity of demand with respect to car travel.

questions.questionText: Weekly sales of doughnuts are 20 000 and the market price is £1.20 per doughnut. The government introduces a new indirect tax of 15p per doughnut. Sales fall to 16 000 a week and the price rises to £1.30 per doughnut. The share of the total weekly tax that is borne by doughnut producers is
Assess the view that high-speed Internet connection is a necessity for modern life and should be provided by the government, free of charge, to all households.

Many goods are sold in plastic packaging that has harmful effects on the environment. In Figure 3, D1 and S1 are the free market demand for and supply of plastic packaged goods. S2 would be the supply if firms took account of the cost to the environment of plastic packaging. The government decides to implement a policy that would result in production moving from the free market level at Q1 to the social optimum at Q2. Which one of the following policies is most likely to achieve the government’s objective?
options: A subsidy at the rate P1 P3
A subsidy at the rate P2 P3
A tax at the rate P2 P1
A tax at the rate P2 P3

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is a reason why the extension of property rights is likely to reduce market failure?
options: Merit goods will no longer be underconsumed in a free market.
Producers will be more likely to have to pay compensation for pollution.
Public goods will no longer be subject to the free-rider problem.
The inequality in the distribution of income and wealth will be reduced.

questions.questionText: After considering Extract D, and the original evidence in Extracts A, B and C, would you recommend that the UK government provides financial and other support to companies involved in the production of commercial aircraft? Justify your recommendation.

Figure 3 shows the demand curve (Demand) and the supply curve (Supply) for bus travel within a city. The initial market equilibrium price is P. To reduce pollution, the city council pays bus companies to provide bus travel free of charge. As a result of this policy, consumer surplus will increase by the area
options: OFHJ
FGH
OPHJ
QHJ

questions.questionText: Figure 6 represents the market for sugar in a country. It shows the demand (D) curve and two supply (S1 and S2) curves in the market for sugar before and after the imposition of an indirect tax on sugar. According to Figure 6, which one of the following combinations: A, B, C, or D, is correct?

After considering Extract E, and the original evidence in Extracts A, B, C and D, which policies, if any, would you recommend that the UK government should introduce to ensure that it achieves its zero-emissions target by 2050. Justify your recommendation.

Extract C (lines 17–19) states: ‘Many environmental economists suggest that making firms pay for the costs of landfill associated with their products, or taxing raw material inputs, will be necessary to ensure a sustainable future for all.’ Using the extracts and your knowledge of economics, evaluate policies, if any, that governments in developed countries should pursue to reduce waste and encourage the recycling of waste products.

Extract F (lines 1–3) states: ‘There are aspects of market failure in the social care sector, though some argue that inappropriate government intervention and a lack of funding are the main reasons why the system is failing to deliver high quality care.’ Using the extracts and your knowledge of economics, assess policies that might be used to improve the provision of social care in the UK.
Which one of the following government policies is most likely to reduce market failure and to improve the allocation of resources?
options: A higher rate of tax on all firms earning profit
A minimum price for demerit goods above their free market price
Free market pricing for the provision of public goods
Subsidies paid to all loss-making firms to maintain full employment

questions.questionText: Figure 6 shows the marginal private and social benefit (MPB and MSB) curves and the marginal private and social cost (MPC and MSC) curves in the market for domestically produced solar panels. The initial market equilibrium is at E1. To correct the market failure, the government introduces a subsidy to domestic manufacturers of solar panels of £200 per unit produced. Which one of the following represents the total amount of subsidy payments made by the government in the first year of the scheme?
options: £20 million.
£25 million.
£75 million.
£100 million.

questions.questionText: A government decides to set a minimum price for plastic bottles of water above the current market price. The most likely impact of the scheme will be
options: a rise in consumption of plastic bottles of water.
a shortage of plastic bottles of water if the price elasticity of supply is zero.
excess stocks of plastic bottles of water.
no excess supply of plastic bottles of water if the price elasticity of demand is zero.

questions.questionText: The following diagram shows the free market supply (S) and demand (D1) for a good when there is imperfect information. D2 shows the level of demand if consumers had full information about the effects of consuming the good. Which one of the following government policies is most likely to result in the social optimum level of consumption?
options: A maximum price equal to P3
A minimum price equal to P2
A subsidy per unit equal to P1 – P2
A tax per unit equal to P3 – P2

questions.questionText: Using the data in Extract D (Figure 3), calculate the amount of government funding per £ of passenger income in the UK rail industry for the year 2015–16. Give your answer correct to the nearest penny.
The following supply and demand diagram shows the impact of a government tax on chocolate bars. The amount of tax revenue raised each week is
options: £0.45 million
£0.60 million
£0.75 million
£1.00 million

questions.questionText: Explain how the impact of a minimum price for a good or service is affected by its price elasticity of demand and its price elasticity of supply.
A government sets a maximum price below the current market price for rented housing. The likely long-run consequence is that
options: fewer people can live in rented housing.
the rationing function of prices will improve.
there will be a fall in supply of owner-occupied housing.
there will be excess supply of rented housing.

questions.questionText: The diagram below shows the market demand (D) curve and two supply (S1 and S2) curves for a brand of soft drink. The drink is a demerit good because of its high sugar content. The government imposes an indirect tax on each can sold that cuts consumption by 100 000 cans per week. If the price elasticity of demand for the drink is –2.0, the price must have increased by
options: 5p

questions.questionText: After considering Extract E, and the original evidence in Extracts A, B, C and D, would you recommend that the Government should increase its spending on housing? Justify your recommendation.
In an economy, competitive firms supply electricity that is generated using coal-fired power stations. If the government tries to reduce pollution by imposing an indirect tax on the firms, this would
options: shift the market demand curve to the left.
shift the market demand curve to the right.
shift the market supply curve to the left.
shift the market supply curve to the right.

questions.questionText: Extract E (lines 14–16) states that ‘The market economy is not going to create the jobs by itself for those workers who are most affected by the change.’ Extract F (lines 4–5) states that ‘taxing productivity-enhancing tools like robots or machines makes no economic sense.’ Use the extracts and your own knowledge of economics to evaluate whether governments should allow markets to respond freely to the opportunities and challenges presented by technological progress, without any state intervention.
Assess the view that regulation is a better policy for dealing with the problem of air pollution than the allocation of property rights or taxation.

In the following diagram D1 shows the market demand for smoke alarms when consumers have imperfect information about the benefits of installing a smoke alarm. If consumers had full information, the market demand for smoke alarms would be D2. Which one of the following policies is most likely to ensure that consumption and production of smoke alarms are at the social optimum level?
options: A maximum price set at P0
A maximum price set at P2
A subsidy per unit equal to P1 – P0
A subsidy per unit equal to P2 – P0

questions.questionText: Which one of the following would generate a short-run disequilibrium with excess supply in the market for Cornish pasties?
options: A minimum price for Cornish pasties is set above the current market price
Higher meat prices increase the cost of producing Cornish pasties
More advertising increases the demand for Cornish pasties
The government levies a new indirect tax on Cornish pasties

questions.questionText: One way to allocate road space in a congested city would be to charge drivers to use the roads. One reason why this policy is likely to result in a more efficient allocation of resources is because
options: incentives to build new roads would be higher.
only higher income drivers would choose to use the roads.
road use would be rationed to drivers who benefit from it the most.
the government would raise a large amount of revenue from drivers.

questions.questionText: The diagram below shows the demand curve (D) and two supply curves (S1 and S2) in the market for renewable energy. The renewable energy market is initially in equilibrium at a price of OH. The government then introduces a subsidy for renewable energy. After the introduction of the subsidy, the total amount of money received by the producers from both consumers and the government is
options: OGME2
OHLE2
OHNME2
OJKE2

questions.questionText: Which one of the following provides a reason for government intervention in a market?
options: Firms in an oligopolistic market may limit price competition.
Market failures can only be corrected by using regulations.
Monopolistically competitive firms earn abnormal profits in the long run.
Public goods are excludable and rival.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following policies is most likely to have an immediate effect in helping to reduce the amount of poverty in the UK?
options: An increase in government subsidies for buyers of electric cars
A shift in the burden of taxation from direct to indirect taxes
Setting a price floor for basic foods
The introduction of a price ceiling for household energy

questions.questionText: The following diagram shows the impact of a government subsidy for recycling waste which shifts the supply curve from S1 to S2. Which one of the following areas measures the cost of the government subsidy?
options: A B C P1
A B D P2
F C D E
P1 C D P2

questions.questionText: Evaluate the view that imposing a tax is the most effective government policy for reducing the market failures arising from overconsumption of unhealthy food and drink.

The diagram below shows the original market demand and supply curves (D1 and S) for loft insulation. Loft insulation reduces energy consumption. The government wishes to meet its energy efficiency target by shifting the market demand curve for loft insulation from D1 to D2. Which one of the following policies is most likely to enable the government to achieve its objective?
options: A decrease in the rate of VAT on domestic gas and electricity used for home heating
A ‘nudge’ to households to install loft insulation by offering to clear lofts of unwanted items if insulation is installed
The introduction of a maximum price for loft insulation
The introduction of a subsidy paid to the firms installing loft insulation

questions.questionText: The diagram below shows the marginal private and social benefit (MPB and MSB) curves and the marginal private and social cost (MPC and MSC) curves in a market where there are positive externalities in production. At the free market equilibrium, market failure occurs. Which one of the following is correct?
options: As a result of this market failure, consumer surplus is reduced by ZXY
As a result of this market failure, there is a deadweight loss to society of P3P1XZ
P1 minus P3 is the subsidy per unit that is required to correct the market failure and achieve the social optimum
The diagonal distance XY shows the amount by which marginal private cost exceeds marginal social cost at OQ2

questions.questionText: The diagram below shows the market demand curve (D) and two market supply (S1 and S2) curves for a good. The initial equilibrium point is at E1. The introduction by the government of an indirect tax per unit of the good results in a new equilibrium at E2. The amount of the indirect tax per unit is measured by the
options: vertical distance FE2.
increase in price P1P2.
the diagonal distance E1E2.
the horizontal distance GE1.
